subject: Workload -> GPU pool matching, throughput guarantees, and discount routing
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: Claire Wong <claire.wong@medalogic.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Workload -> GPU pool matching, throughput guarantees, and discount routing

Hi Claire —

Thanks for sharing the workload extract. I pulled together an initial right-size recommendation and a pricing/packaging path you can share with Procurement. Summary up front: based on the CSV you sent, we recommend a 6-GPU reserved pool (NVIDIA A100 equivalent) with a 20% burst buffer that covers your peak windows, paired with a 99th pct latency SLO of 350ms for 1k-token generations. High level rationale and assumptions below. Attachment: redwood-dedicated-proposal-v3.pdf (proposal + SLAs) and medalogic-workload-metrics.csv (ingested).

Workload assumptions (from your CSV)
- Average QPS (24h): 120 RPS
- Peak QPS (5-min window): 450 RPS
- Average response tokens per request: ~420 tokens (includes prompt + response)
- Typical context length: 1.2k tokens for multistep workflows; median context ~800 tokens
- Concurrency pattern: long tail (90% small, 10% heavy requests), estimated concurrency needs = 40-60 concurrent active streams at peak

Sizing rationale
- Baseline GPU count: 6x A100-equivalent for steady-state to meet sustained 120 RPS with average context.
- Burst buffer: add 20% capacity (effectively ~1.2x) to absorb short peaks — addresses 5-min peaks up to ~540 RPS without immediate autoscale.
- Latency / SLO: targeting p95 < 200ms for short prompts and p99 < 350ms for the 1k+ token tails given batching and KV cache enabled.
- Headroom for model mix: if you plan to run both a 13B and a 70B variant concurrently, we recommend reserving an additional 1-2 GPUs for routing compatibility or use an on-demand fallback for the 70B workload.

Commit + pricing path (packaging options)
- Option A (standard reserved commit): 12-month reserved commitment for 6 GPUs. Pricing delta from on-demand: ~28% discount.
- Option B (annual elevated commit): 12-month reserved commit for 8 GPUs with 18% discount + one-time onboarding credit covering first-month usage. Good if you expect sustained growth or want guaranteed throughput headroom.
- Option C (pilot -> scale): 3-month trial with 4 GPUs reserved + burst credits to simulate peak traffic, then convert to a 12-month commit at month 3 with a tailored discount based on measured consumption.

Open questions for procurement and engineering
1) Do you need a hard throughput guarantee (SLA-backed) or is a best-effort latency target with credits acceptable?
2) What percentage of requests must be served by the reserved pool vs. on-demand (helps finalize commit size)?
3) Will you accept a model-fallback policy for oversized requests (70B runs on on-demand with routing to reserved for <13B)?

If you want, Ben can draft a short commercial term sheet we can hand to Procurement that lays out the commit numbers, discount tiers, and trial mechanics.

Next step: propose a 30-minute call Monday to review the price/commit options and run a quick 5-min throughput simulation with your CSV.

Best,
Maya

Maya Srinivasan
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Claire Wong <claire.wong@medalogic.com>

Date: Sun, 01 Nov 2026 09:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Workload -> GPU pool matching, throughput guarantees, and discount routing

Maya —

Thanks for the detailed write-up and for pulling numbers from our export. A few clarifying questions before we loop Procurement:

1) Burst behaviour: when you say 20% burst buffer — does that mean short bursts are consumed from reserved pool credits or is the burst served from on-demand capacity?
2) If we choose Option B (8 GPUs), what is the expected token cost (per 1M tokens) on committed pricing vs our current cloud spend? Procurement will ask for a delta in $/1M tokens.
3) SLAs: we need to understand what happens if p99 latency slips beyond 350ms for a week. Is there a service credit?

Also scheduling note — Monday morning PST works for me. Can Ben join to go over commercial numbers?

Thanks,
Claire

Claire Wong
Head of AI Platform, Medalogic
claire.wong@medalogic.com | +1 212-555-0199
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Claire Wong <claire.wong@medalogic.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Workload -> GPU pool matching, throughput guarantees, and discount routing

Claire —

Happy to join Monday — thanks for the prompt questions. Quick answers and a commercial sketch you can share with Procurement:

Burst mechanics
- Short bursts are covered by reserved pool burst credits first (we allocate a burst pool that smooths 5-15 minute spikes). If the burst pool is exhausted, traffic fails over to on-demand with prioritized routing; the customer only pays on-demand rates for overspill.

Token cost examples (ballpark — final will be in the term sheet)
- Committed 6-GPU, 12-mo: ~$420 per 1M tokens (weighted average across model mix — 13B dominant).
- Committed 8-GPU, 12-mo: ~$370 per 1M tokens (improved unit economics because of higher commit).
- On-demand overspill: ~$520 per 1M tokens.

SLA / credits
- We offer a p99 latency SLO with a service credit ladder: 5% credit for failing p99 SLA in a month, 10% for two consecutive months, and an escalation path to an engineering review. We can discuss a custom credit formula for Enterprise terms.

Discount routing idea
- If Procurement prefers a lower headline commit, we can propose a blended approach: 12-mo commit at 6 GPUs at the 28% discount, plus a volume-based rebate once total token consumption exceeds X over 12 months (rebate applied retroactively). That gets you closer to the 8-GPU unit cost without locking the extra capacity upfront.

I can produce a short term sheet with exact $ numbers, payment cadence (monthly vs quarterly), and onboarding credits. Maya / Priya: can you confirm the expected model mix (percent 70B vs 13B) so I can finalize the $/1M token calc?

-Ben

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 646-555-0182
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Claire Wong <claire.wong@medalogic.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Workload -> GPU pool matching, throughput guarantees, and discount routing

Claire, Ben —

Following up with the model-mix and a short mutual action plan so Procurement and your infra team have clear next steps.

Model mix (Medalogic inputs / recommended routing)
- 85% of requests estimated on 13B-class model (default path).
- 12% of requests higher-accuracy 70B variant (route to on-demand by default) — we can route low-latency 70B inference to reserved if you increase commit.
- 3% experimental / batch jobs (scheduled off-peak).

Recommended near-term commit: Option A -> start with 6 GPUs reserved, enable a 20% burst credit buffer, and run a 60-day telemetry review. If measured peak overspill exceeds 12% of total tokens in the first 30 days, convert to the 8-GPU elevated commit (Option B) with back-dated rebate applied for the month conversion happens.

Mutual action plan (MAP)
- Day 0: Legal / Procurement review term sheet (Ben to send).
- Day 0-7: Set up VPC peering and IAM roles; exchange SSO and KMS scope doc.
- Day 7-14: Pilot ingest — route 100% of non-production traffic to reserved pool; collect telemetry (p95/p99, token counts, concurrency).
- Day 30: Exec sync to review telemetry; decide on Option B conversion if overspill >12%
- Day 60: Finalize annual commit and sign DocuSign.

Claire — let me know if Procurement wants the term sheet to include a revenue-protected cap or a minimum monthly invoice. Ben, I added the ticket to our internal repo to create sample SLO language for the term sheet.

Thanks,
Priya
